clue.text: Oddly enough they're usually put in to bowl

definitions.text: Oddly enough they're usually put in to bowl

parts.words: Oddly enough they're usually put in to bowl
parts.note: reads as cricketers sent in to bowl, though in cricket the side put in bats; the other sense is the cake mixtures poured into a mixing bowl

explanation.surface: A cricket paradox: the side sent in seems always to be the one that bowls.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the team 'put in' bats, so it seems odd; but the batters here are mixtures of flour, egg and milk, which are poured into a bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Batter is a pancake or cake mixture, beaten in a bowl, and cricket also calls its strikers by this name.

clue.text: Stage to get a playful kiss on the head?

parts.note: buss is an old word for a kiss
the top is the head of something

explanation.surface: Getting a light kiss on the head at some point.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'stage' is a fare stage, where a bus picks up passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A fare stage is the point where a bus stops, so a bus stop.

clue.text: Where scores, often converted, take note on the Adriatic

parts.note: in rugby a try is a score often followed by a conversion kick
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Where rugby tries are scored and musical notes are taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where' introduces the definition: a place on the Adriatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Trieste is an Italian port on the Adriatic Sea.

clue.text: Cross-Channel apathy

parts.note: listlessness as named across the English Channel, that is in French

explanation.surface: Indifference on the other side of the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross-Channel' means French: the English word is borrowed from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, a French word taken into English.

clue.text: Hertfordshire town theatre holding another 22

indicators.note: the theatre word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: the stage stands for the theatre
22-across means flat, and another word for it is even

explanation.surface: A town's theatre containing another production.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 refers to 22-across, LEVEL; 'another 22' is a synonym of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenage is a new town in Hertfordshire, north of London.

clue.text: Lady without rival when around fifty

indicators.note: the clue says the answer becomes the 'without rival' word when it goes around the Roman fifty, so take that letter out

parts.note: peerless means having no equal
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A woman who has no rival once she reaches her fifties.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: put the answer around L and you get PEERLESS ('without rival'), so remove L from PEERLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeress is a woman holding a title of nobility, or a peer's wife, so a titled lady.

clue.text: Pastry taking one's breath away?

definitions.meaning: light cream pastries, as in cream cakes
pants or gasps, as one does when out of breath

explanation.surface: A pastry so good it leaves you breathless.
explanation.definitionFit: Puffs are light pastries, and puffing is breathing hard.

clue.text: His duties might be an eye- opener to scattered Mexicans

definitions.note: the man whose duties are excise duties

indicators.note: an opener comes first, so take the first letter of eye
scattered means spread about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An official's tax demands would shock some Mexicans.
explanation.definitionFit: An exciseman collected excise duties, the taxes on goods such as spirits.

clue.text: C 7 A state that turns me livid

indicators.note: turns means the word me is turned round

parts.note: livid means furious, or irate

explanation.surface: A country whose ways make me furious.
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is a state ruled by an emir.

clue.text: Time device laid student body up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole run is read from the bottom

parts.note: taken as written
NUS is the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: A clock laid out the student union.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundial tells the hour by a shadow cast by the sun.

clue.text: Novel idea of remote planetary life? Matter of fact, it isn't

definitions.text: Novel idea of remote planetary life?

parts.note: science is the study of what is factually so
fiction is what is not true

explanation.surface: Is life on distant planets a fact or a fantasy?
explanation.walkthrough: The two halves of the genre name are defined separately: established knowledge, then made-up story.
explanation.definitionFit: The genre of novels imagining alien worlds and future technology.

clue.text: See 9
Irritability displayed on being excluded from inter nationals?

definitions.text: Irritability displayed on being excluded from inter nationals?

parts.words: Irritability displayed on being excluded from inter nationals?
parts.note: a player dropped from international Test matches would be irritable, and the answer splits as a pun on 'Test'

explanation.surface: A player sulks after being left out of the national side.
explanation.walkthrough: Test matches are cricket internationals; the answer begins with TEST, hinting at the grumpiness of a player left out of the Tests.
explanation.definitionFit: Being irritable and easily annoyed is the same as being short-tempered.

clue.text: Ashipwreckedoldcavalry man

indicators.note: a wrecked ship is broken apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shipwreck involving a veteran horseman.
explanation.definitionFit: A spahi was a cavalry trooper of the Ottoman empire or of French Algerian units.

clue.text: Portion of baked food around the City

indicators.note: the baked item goes around the City's postcode letters

parts.note: a pie is baked food
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A slice of pastry bought in the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a part or share of something, as is a portion.

clue.text: Excellent motto for those on a the up-and-up

definitions.text: Excellent motto for those on a the up-and-up

parts.words: Excellent motto for those on a the up-and-up
parts.note: a Latin word meaning higher, an apt slogan for climbers, and also used to mean first-class

explanation.surface: A slogan for people who are rising in life.
explanation.definitionFit: Excelsior is Latin for higher, the motto of New York State.

clue.text: Sounds for a start of all marble design

indicators.note: a design is a fresh arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A marble pattern used to begin something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' means a jolt of alarm, not a beginning: the device rings out to startle.
explanation.definitionFit: A warning bell rings to raise an alert, giving people a fright.

clue.text: He gets what coming to him every year

definitions.text: He gets what coming to him every year

parts.words: He gets what coming to him every year
parts.note: someone receiving a yearly payment gets what is due annually

explanation.surface: A man getting his just deserts every year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets what's coming to him' sounds like punishment, but here it is a regular payment.
explanation.definitionFit: An annuitant is a person who receives a yearly allowance.

clue.text: Confess one could do with a bath?

definitions.meaning: to own up and tell the truth

definitions.text: one could do with a bath?
definitions.meaning: taken literally, someone who needs a wash might arrive in a washed state

explanation.surface: An admission from someone in need of a wash.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming clean is an idiom for admitting the truth; literally it is arriving washed.

clue.text: Sedative to relax a busybody

parts.note: to calm is to soothe or relax
an ant is a proverbially busy body

explanation.surface: A sedative to soothe a meddler.
explanation.definitionFit: A calmant is a calming drug, a tranquilliser.

clue.text: Certainly not fast to overhaul decoration of President Reagan's office

indicators.note: to overhaul something is to rework it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: MBE is a British honour
the Oval Office is the US President's office

explanation.surface: A slow overhaul of the décor of the White House office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' means fixed firmly, not quick; MBE is Member of the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Something movable is not fixed in place.

clue.text: Desert region recalling first-rate cake

indicators.note: recalling means calling back, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate
a bun is a small cake

explanation.surface: A desert area remembered for an excellent cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubia is the ancient region along the Nile in Sudan and southern Egypt, much of it desert.

clue.text: Telephones for the fans ?

explanation.surface: Phones for the supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: Blower is old British slang for a phone; a fan pushes air around.

clue.text: Finds sea-legs in no time

indicators.note: the letters find a new arrangement, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor finds his balance at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in no time' looks like 'quickly' but means outside time, timeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ageless is untouched by time, timeless.

clue.text: It's even reversible too

indicators.note: the word reads the same in both directions, so it can be reversed

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A remark that something is balanced and can be turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Level means flat or equal, the same as even.

clue.text: Impress, not necessarily one's own family

definitions.meaning: to make someone fully realise something
the phrase also means to take a guest back to your house, who need not be a relative

explanation.surface: Making an impression on a family that may not be yours.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something home to someone is an idiom for making them grasp it; literally it is taking a person back to your house.

clue.text: Could be an attachment for an Eastern lady

parts.note: be is the verb from could be
gum attaches things

explanation.surface: An accessory suitable for an Eastern woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A begum is a Muslim woman of high rank in South Asia.

clue.text: Legionnaire's exploit sounds a joke

indicators.note: sounds says the word is heard aloud, like a joke

parts.note: a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: A soldier's heroics sound like a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: Beau Geste is the novel about the French Foreign Legion.
explanation.definitionFit: A geste is a heroic deed, as in Beau Geste.

clue.text: Heather follows a physician in no hurry

indicators.note: the heather word comes after the other pieces

parts.note: MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a physician's degree
ling is a kind of heather

explanation.surface: A girl named Heather comes after the doctor, unhurried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambling is walking at a slow, easy pace.

clue.text: Severe wind south by east

parts.note: Auster is the Latin name for the south wind

explanation.surface: A harsh wind blowing from the south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means stern and strict, just like severe.

clue.text: Proposition giving the alternative to me in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
or introduces an alternative

indicators.note: in reverse says the word me is read backwards

explanation.surface: Offering an option, then turning back to oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a statement proved by reasoning, a mathematical proposition.

clue.text: Locks ahead for a vessel shrouded by trees

indicators.note: being shrouded means being wrapped, so the ship goes inside the trees

parts.note: taken as written
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Locks ahead for a ship hidden among woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' suggests canal locks ahead of a vessel; it means hair, and 'ahead for' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Tresses are long locks of hair.
